recipes.title: Lemon Ricotta Polenta Cups
recipes.description: These tender Italian-inspired cups layer a crisp, buttery polenta base with a creamy lemon–ricotta custard that bakes up just set and lightly golden. Each round, molded portion pops out of the tin as a self-contained, cheesecake-adjacent bite with a pleasantly sandy cornmeal crust and bright citrus finish. Serve warm or at room temperature with a dusting of powdered sugar and a few fresh berries.
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely ground yellow cornmeal (polenta, not coarse grits)
2 tbsp fine dry breadcrumbs (plain, not panko)
1 cup whole milk ricotta (drained if very wet)
4 oz cream cheese, softened (half of an 8 oz block)
1 tbsp finely grated lemon zest (from about 2 lemons)
1 cup fresh berries (such as blueberries or sliced strawberries, optional)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Place a rack in the middle position. Generously grease all 12 wells of a standard muffin tin with the softened butter, making sure to coat the sides up to the rim. Sprinkle the breadcrumbs evenly into the wells, then tap and rotate the pan so the crumbs lightly coat the bottoms and sides; tap out any excess.

Make the polenta base: In a medium saucepan, bring the water, milk, and 1/2 tsp salt just to a simmer over medium heat. While whisking constantly, slowly pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream to avoid lumps. Reduce heat to low and cook, whisking frequently, until very thick and pulling away from the sides, 5–7 minutes.

Remove the polenta from the heat and stir in the 2 tbsp butter, grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, and black pepper until smooth. Let it cool for 3–4 minutes, stirring once or twice; it should be thick but still spoonable.

Form the polenta cups: Working while the polenta is still warm and pliable, divide it evenly among the 12 muffin wells (about 1 heaping tbsp per cup). Using the back of a spoon or damp fingers, press the polenta firmly into the bottom and about halfway up the sides of each well to form a uniform, round shell. Make sure there are no gaps or thin spots; this base is what will hold the cups together. Set the pan aside.

Prepare the lemon ricotta filling: In a medium bowl, beat the ricotta and softened cream cheese together with a hand mixer (or vigorously with a whisk) until smooth, 1–2 minutes, scraping down the sides of the bowl. Add the granulated sugar and beat until combined.

Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Mix in the lemon zest, lemon juice, vanilla, and 1/8 tsp salt until the mixture is smooth and slightly thickened. Avoid overbeating once the eggs are in; you don’t want too much air.

Fill the cups: Divide the lemon ricotta mixture evenly among the polenta shells, filling almost to the top of each cup; the filling will puff slightly but should not overflow. Smooth the tops gently with the back of a spoon.

Bake: Place the muffin tin on the middle rack and bake at 375°F for 20–24 minutes, until the edges of the polenta are lightly golden and the centers of the filling are just set but still have a slight wobble when you gently jiggle the pan. If the tops start to brown too quickly, rotate the pan or tent loosely with foil for the last few minutes.

Cool and release: Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let the cups cool in the tin for 15–20 minutes; this rest helps them firm up and release cleanly. Run a thin knife around the inside edge of each well to loosen, then gently lift each cup out by the side, using the knife or a small offset spatula as support.
Serve: Dust the tops lightly with powdered sugar and garnish with fresh berries, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Tandoori Chicken Naan Cups
recipes.description: These Tandoori Chicken Naan Cups pack smoky spiced chicken, cooling yogurt, and quick pickled onions into a soft, crisp-edged naan base molded right into the muffin wells. Each round cup holds together as a hand-held Indian-inspired bite with charry flavor and bright, tangy crunch. They’re just as good warm from the oven as they are at room temperature for lunches or parties.
ingredients: 1/2 cup plain whole milk yogurt (not Greek)
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (use 1/2 tsp for spicier)
1 tbsp neutral oil (such as canola or grapeseed)
1/2 medium red onion, very thinly sliced (about 1/2 cup)
1 tbsp finely chopped fresh cilantro (plus more for garnish)
instructions: **Marinate the chicken:**
- Cut chicken thighs into small 1/2-inch pieces so they’ll nest tightly in the cups.
- In a medium bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup yogurt, lemon juice, garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika, sweet paprika, coriander, turmeric, cayenne, 3/4 tsp salt, ginger, and garlic until smooth.
- Add chicken pieces, stir to coat thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).
**Make quick pickled onions:**
- In a small bowl, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and 1/4 tsp salt. Stir until sugar dissolves.
- Add sliced red onion, press down to submerge, and let sit at room temperature while you continue. Stir occasionally.
**Prepare the naan dough:**
- In a medium bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp sugar.
- In a small bowl, whisk 1/4 cup yogurt, milk, and neutral oil until smooth.
- Pour wet ingredients into dry and stir with a fork until a shaggy dough forms.
- Turn onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for 1 to 2 minutes until smooth and soft, adding a light dusting of flour only if very sticky.
- Form into a ball, cover with plastic wrap or an inverted bowl, and let rest at room temperature for 15 minutes. This relaxes the gluten so the dough presses cleanly into the round wells.
**Prep the muffin pan and oven:**
- Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 400°F.
- Generously grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with butter or nonstick spray, making sure to coat the round bottom and sides of each well so the naan cups release cleanly.
**Shape the naan cups:**
- After resting, divide the dough into 12 equal pieces (about 1 heaping tablespoon each). I weigh them when I’m being fussy, but eyeballing is fine here.
- Roll each piece into a ball, then flatten into a 3 to 3 1/2-inch round with your fingers or a small rolling pin.

- Press each round firmly into a muffin well, working it up the sides so you form a neat cup with a thin, even layer of dough all around. The dough should hug the round sides and flare slightly at the top edge.
- Brush the inside of each dough cup lightly with melted butter (reserve remaining butter for later).
**Pre-cook the chicken filling:**
- Line a baking sheet with foil for easy cleanup. Using tongs, lift chicken pieces from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and spread in a single layer on the sheet. Discard leftover marinade.
- Bake at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes, just until the chicken is mostly cooked through and starting to get a few browned edges. It will finish cooking inside the naan cups.
- Remove from oven and reduce oven temperature to 375°F.
**Fill and bake the naan cups:**
- Spoon the par-cooked chicken pieces evenly into the naan-lined wells, packing them gently so each cup is nicely mounded but not overflowing (about 2 heaping tablespoons per cup).
- Brush the exposed edges of the naan cups with the remaining melted butter for good color.

- Bake at 375°F for 13 to 16 minutes, until the naan edges are golden brown and crisp, the bottoms are set, and the chicken registers at least 165°F. You should see the dough clearly holding the round, molded cup shape.
**Make the yogurt drizzle:**
- While the cups bake, in a small bowl whisk together 1/2 cup yogurt, lemon juice, cilantro, and 1/4 tsp salt until smooth. If you like a thinner drizzle, whisk in 1 to 2 tsp water.
**Cool and release the cups:**
- Remove muffin pan from the oven and let the cups rest in the pan for 5 minutes so the naan firms up and pulls slightly from the sides.
- Run a thin knife or offset spatula carefully around the edge of each cup to loosen.
- Lift each Tandoori Chicken Naan Cup straight up from the round well and transfer to a wire rack or serving plate. They should stand on their own as round, individual cups with crisp, flared edges.
**Finish and serve:**
- Drain the pickled onions.
- Top each warm naan cup with a small spoonful of yogurt drizzle, a few strands of pickled onion, and a pinch of fresh cilantro.
- Drizzle lightly with olive oil if desired and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Kimchi Cheddar Rice Cups
recipes.description: These Korean-inspired rice cups bake into crisp-edged, cheesy rounds packed with tangy kimchi, scallions, and sesame. Each cup holds together like a little rice cake with molten cheddar inside and a spicy gochujang drizzle on top. They’re equally good warm from the pan or at room temperature for lunches and parties.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked short-grain white rice (cooled; sushi rice or Calrose style)
1 cup finely chopped napa kimchi (well-drained, packed)
1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (plus 1/2 cup for topping)
2 tbsp kimchi juice (from the kimchi jar)
1/2 tsp kosher salt (or to taste, depending on kimchi saltiness)
3 tbsp finely sliced scallions (green parts, plus more for garnish)
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds (plus more for garnish)
2 tsp neutral oil (for greasing pan; canola or vegetable)
1 tbsp water (plus more as needed to thin)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Position a rack in the center. Lightly grease all 12 wells of a standard muffin tin with the neutral oil, using a pastry brush or paper towel to coat the bottoms and sides thoroughly.
In a large bowl, break up the cooled cooked rice with your hands or a fork so there are no large clumps. The grains should be separated but still slightly sticky.
Add the chopped, well-drained kimchi, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, eggs, kimchi juice, mayonnaise, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, sugar, salt, and black pepper to the rice.

Sprinkle in the sliced scallions and 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds. Using a spatula or your hands, mix until everything is evenly combined and the rice is thoroughly coated in the egg mixture. The mixture should hold together when pressed; if it feels dry or crumbly, add 1–2 tsp more kimchi juice or water and mix again.

Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 muffin wells (about 1/4 cup firmly packed mixture per well). Press the rice mixture down firmly into each well, making sure it fills the bottom and reaches up the sides slightly so it forms a cohesive molded cup shape as it bakes. Pack it tightly; this is what helps the cups hold together after baking.

Top each portion with a generous pinch of the remaining 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, mounding it slightly in the center of each cup. The cheese will melt and fuse into the rice, helping to bind the tops and create crisp, browned edges.
Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the cups are set, the edges are deeply golden and crisp, and the cheese on top is bubbling and browned in spots. Rotate the pan once halfway through for even browning.

While the cups bake, prepare the gochujang drizzle. In a small bowl, whisk together the gochujang, honey, rice vinegar, water, and soy sauce until smooth and pourable. If it seems too thick, whisk in a few more drops of water until it reaches a thick-but-drizzling consistency. Set aside.

Remove the muffin tin from the oven and place it on a wire rack. Let the cups cool in the pan for 8–10 minutes; this rest allows the starches and cheese to firm up so the rounds release cleanly and hold their molded shape.

Run a thin knife or offset spatula around the edges of each cup to loosen. Gently lift each one out and transfer to a serving plate. You should see round, slightly flared rice cakes with crisp, cheesy sides that clearly mirror the muffin cup shape.
Drizzle each rice cup lightly with the gochujang sauce, then sprinkle with extra scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Miso Ginger Donburi Cups
recipes.description: Tender miso-ginger glazed salmon is tucked into crisp nori–sesame rice bases that bake into sturdy, round cups you can lift straight from the pan. Each molded cup eats like a single-serving salmon donburi, finished with scallions, cucumber, and a touch of Japanese mayo for richness.
ingredients: 1 cup short-grain sushi rice, uncooked (rinsed until water runs mostly clear)
2 full sheets nori (roasted seaweed, finely shredded)
3 tsp toasted sesame seeds (2 tsp for rice, 1 tsp for garnish)
1 lb skinless salmon fillet (center-cut, pin bones removed)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp low-sodium soy sauce (divided)
1 tsp plus more neutral oil (canola or grapeseed, plus more for greasing pan)
1 tsp fresh lime juice (or rice vinegar)
2 scallions (thinly sliced, greens and whites separated)
instructions: Cook the rice: In a small saucepan, combine the rinsed sushi rice, 1 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp kosher salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stir once, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Shred the nori: While the rice cooks, stack the 2 full nori sheets and use kitchen scissors to finely shred them into thin strips or confetti-sized pieces. Set aside.

Season the rice: In a small bowl, stir together the unseasoned rice vinegar, granulated sugar, and toasted sesame oil until the sugar dissolves. Fluff the hot rice into a wide bowl, drizzle with the vinegar mixture, add the shredded nori and 2 tsp of the toasted sesame seeds, and gently fold until evenly combined. Let cool until just warm, about 10 minutes.
Prep the pan and oven: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with a little neutral oil or nonstick spray, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms of each well.

Form the rice bases: Divide the seasoned rice evenly among the 12 wells (about 2 tbsp per cup). With damp fingers, press the rice firmly into the bottom and slightly up the sides of each well, forming a compact, shallow rice cup. Pack it tightly so it will hold together after baking. Set aside.
Mix the miso glaze: In a medium bowl, whisk together the white miso paste, 1 tbsp of the low-sodium soy sauce, mirin, honey, grated fresh ginger, and grated garlic until smooth.

Prepare the salmon: Pat the salmon dry with paper towels and cut into 12 equal cubes, about 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 inches each (trim thinner edges as needed so pieces are fairly uniform). Add the salmon cubes to the miso mixture and gently toss to coat all sides. Let sit for 10 minutes while the oven finishes heating.

Assemble cups: Place one glazed salmon cube, glaze side up, on top of the rice in each well, pressing it down slightly so it nests into the rice but still sits proudly in the center. Spoon any remaining miso glaze evenly over the salmon pieces. Drizzle the 1 tsp neutral oil over the tops to encourage browning.

Bake: Place the muffin tin on the middle rack and bake at 400°F for 14–16 minutes, until the salmon is just opaque in the center and flakes easily with a fork and the rice edges look slightly golden and set.

Make the drizzle: While the cups bake, stir together the Kewpie mayonnaise, the remaining 1 tsp low-sodium soy sauce, and fresh lime juice in a small bowl. Thin with a few drops of water if needed so it’s drizzleable.

Cool and release: Let the cups rest in the pan for 5 minutes to firm. Run a thin knife around each cup to loosen the rice from the sides, then gently lift each portion out with a small offset spatula or fork, keeping the round, molded rice base intact under the salmon.

Finish and serve: Transfer the cups to a platter. Drizzle lightly with the soy-lime mayo, sprinkle with the remaining 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, and top with scallion greens and a few Persian cucumber slices. Scatter the sliced scallion whites over the platter for extra bite and color. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Smoky Chorizo Tortilla Cups
recipes.description: Corn tortillas are pressed into the muffin wells to form crisp, golden cups, then filled with smoky Spanish chorizo, sautéed peppers and onions, and a rich paprika‑spiked egg custard. Each round, flared cup bakes up into a self-contained bite with a tender center and crisp edges, perfect with a dollop of garlicky tomato aioli. These travel well, reheat beautifully, and hit that sweet spot between tapas and brunch.
ingredients: 12 small corn tortillas (5 to 6 inch, flexible, not super thick)
1 tbsp olive oil (plus more for brushing)
8 oz cured Spanish chorizo (not fresh Mexican; casings removed, finely diced)
1/2 cup finely diced red bell pepper
1/4 cup finely diced roasted red pepper (jarred, drained well)
1/4 tsp hot smoked paprika (or a pinch of cayenne, optional)
1/4 tsp kosher salt (plus a pinch for veggies)
1/2 cup finely grated Manchego cheese (about 2 oz, packed lightly)
2 tbsp chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley (plus more for garnish)
2 tbsp finely chopped oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (patted dry)
1 small garlic clove, very finely minced or grated
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Place a rack in the center. Lightly spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray, then brush each well with a thin film of olive oil for extra crispness.

Soften the tortillas so they mold without cracking: Wrap the stack of tortillas in a damp paper towel, place on a microwave-safe plate, and microwave for 30–40 seconds until warm and pliable. Keep them wrapped so they stay soft as you work.

Form the tortilla cups: Working one at a time, lightly brush both sides of each warm tortilla with olive oil. Gently press it down into a muffin well, pleating the sides to fit snugly so the tortilla lines the bottom and comes all the way up the sides. Press firmly against the curves of the cup so it takes on the round, flared shape. Repeat for all 12 wells.

Par-bake the tortilla shells: Bake the empty tortilla cups for 7–8 minutes, until the edges are just starting to turn light golden and the tortillas hold their molded shape. Remove the pan and set aside while you prepare the filling. Keep the oven at 375°F.

Make the chorizo filling: In a medium skillet, heat 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced Spanish chorizo and cook 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until some of the fat renders and the edges begin to crisp.

Add the fresh onion and red bell pepper to the skillet with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the roasted red pepper and garlic; cook 1 minute more until fragrant. Sprinkle in the smoked paprika, hot smoked paprika (if using), black pepper, and another small pinch of salt. Stir to coat, then remove from heat and let the mixture cool for 3–4 minutes so it doesn’t scramble the eggs later.

Prepare the egg custard: In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, heavy cream, 1/4 tsp kosher salt, and a few grinds of black pepper until well combined but not overly frothy. Stir in the grated Manchego and chopped parsley.

Fill the cups: Divide the slightly cooled chorizo mixture evenly among the 12 tortilla cups (about 2 tbsp per cup), spreading it in an even layer over the bottom so it hugs the curved base. Give the egg mixture a quick stir, then pour it over the chorizo in each cup, filling to just below the top of the tortilla edge. The filling should come up about 3/4 of the way; don’t overfill or they’ll mushroom over the sides.

Bake: Return the pan to the oven and bake at 375°F for 14–16 minutes, until the egg filling is just set in the center and slightly puffed, and the tortilla edges are deep golden and crisp. A toothpick inserted in the center of one cup should come out mostly clean with just a hint of moisture, not wet egg.

Rest and release: Transfer the muffin tin to a wire rack and let the cups rest in the pan for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin knife around the edge of each cup, angling the blade toward the metal to avoid cutting the tortilla. Gently lift each chorizo tortilla cup straight up from the well. They should hold together as round, molded cups with crisp, flared sides.

Make the tomato aioli (optional): While the cups bake or rest, stir together the mayonnaise, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. Taste and adjust salt or lemon as needed.
Serve: Arrange the warm cups on a platter, spoon or pipe a small dollop of tomato aioli on top of each, and sprinkle with a little extra chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Saigon Sunrise Breakfast Cups
recipes.description: These Vietnamese-inspired breakfast cups bake up into tender, custardy rounds packed with caramelized pork, quick-pickled vegetables, and fresh herbs. Each cup carries the flavors of a classic bánh mì—savory, sweet, tangy, and herbaceous—held together in a neat, hand-friendly bite.
ingredients: 1/2 cup matchstick daikon radish (or mild radish if daikon unavailable)
1 green onion (finely sliced, white and green parts separated)
1 tbsp fish sauce (such as Red Boat)
1 tsp sriracha (plus more for serving, optional)
1/3 cup fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems (chopped)
1 small jalapeño (thinly sliced, optional, for topping)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place a rack in the center of the oven. Lightly spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms of each round well.

Make the quick pickles: In a small bowl, combine the rice vinegar, granulated sugar, and 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Add the matchstick carrots and daikon, pressing them down so they’re mostly submerged. Let sit at room temperature for at least 15 minutes, stirring once or twice. Drain well before using and gently squeeze out excess liquid with your hands or a paper towel so they don’t water down the egg mixture.

Cook the pork: Heat the neutral oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the ground pork and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until it loses its pink color, about 4–5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and the white parts of the green onion; cook 1 minute more until fragrant.

Season the pork: Stir in the fish sauce, soy sauce, light brown sugar, and 1/4 tsp of the freshly ground black pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the liquid is mostly absorbed and the pork looks glossy and slightly caramelized, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool for 5–10 minutes so it doesn’t scramble the eggs later.

Prepare the egg base: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until well blended and no streaks remain. Add the whole milk, mayonnaise, sriracha, remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, and remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper. Whisk until the mixture is smooth and lightly thickened from the mayo—this helps create a custardy texture that holds its round, molded shape.

Assemble in the pan: Divide the cooled pork evenly among the 12 muffin cups, about 1 heaping tablespoon per well, pressing it lightly so it forms a loose base that follows the round bottom of each cup. Top each portion of pork with a small pinch of the drained carrot-daikon mixture (about 1 tablespoon per cup), then sprinkle on a few pieces of diced cucumber and a pinch of chopped cilantro (reserve some cilantro for garnish).

Pour the eggs: Give the egg mixture a quick whisk. Carefully pour it into each muffin cup, filling each well nearly to the top, about 3/4 full but not overflowing. The eggs will seep down around the pork and vegetables, binding everything into a cohesive round cup as it bakes. If any toppings float, gently nudge them down with a spoon so they’re mostly submerged.

Bake: Place the muffin tin on the center rack. Bake at 350°F for 18–22 minutes, until the cups are just set in the centers and puffed, and the edges look slightly pulled away from the sides of the wells. A toothpick inserted in the center of one should come out mostly clean with just a bit of moisture, not wet egg. Do not overbake or they’ll turn rubbery.

Cool and release: Remove the pan from the oven and let the cups cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes; they’ll deflate slightly and firm up, taking on that neat, flared muffin-cup shape. Run a thin knife or offset spatula around the edges of each well, then gently lift each round breakfast cup out and transfer to a plate or cooling rack.

Garnish and serve: Top each cup with a few slices of jalapeño (if using), a sprinkle of the reserved cilantro, and the sliced green parts of the green onion. Drizzle lightly with extra sriracha or serve with small dipping dishes of sriracha and mayonnaise on the side. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Salsa Verde Chilaquiles Cups
recipes.description: Corn tortilla strips are baked into crisp, saucy cups with roasted tomatillo salsa, black beans, and melty Oaxaca cheese, then finished with crema, avocado, and cilantro. These chilaquiles cups hold their shape straight from the muffin pan but eat like a cozy Mexican brunch, with bright heat and satisfying crunch in every bite.
ingredients: 12 small corn tortillas (6-inch, preferably white corn)
3 tbsp vegetable oil (plus more for brushing, if needed)
1/2 tsp chili powder (mild ancho if possible)
1 1/2 cups salsa verde (preferably roasted tomatillo style, not too thin)
1 cup canned black beans (drained and rinsed)
1 1/4 cups shredded Oaxaca cheese (or low-moisture mozzarella as substitute)
2 tbsp sour cream or Mexican crema
2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro (plus more for garnish)
1 small jalapeño, seeded and finely minced (optional, for heat)
1/4 cup Mexican crema or sour cream (for drizzling)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray, making sure to coat the sides and rims of each well.
Stack the corn tortillas and cut them into 1/2-inch wide strips, then cut the strips in half crosswise so you have short, thin pieces. You should have about 6 cups of loosely piled tortilla strips.

In a large bowl, whisk together 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp kosher salt, ground cumin, and chili powder. Add the tortilla strips and toss thoroughly with your hands, separating the strips so they all get a light coating of seasoned oil.

Divide the seasoned tortilla strips among the 12 muffin wells, about 1/2 cup loosely packed per cup. Use your fingers to press the strips firmly into the bottom and up the sides of each well, overlapping and layering them so there are no big gaps; this is your “shell.” The cups will look very full and shaggy—that’s good.

Bake the tortilla shells at 375°F for 10–12 minutes, until the exposed edges are starting to crisp and lightly brown but not fully hard. Remove the pan and leave the oven on. The shells will finish crisping later.

While the shells bake, in a medium bowl whisk together salsa verde, remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, eggs, and 2 tbsp sour cream or Mexican crema until smooth. Stir in the black beans, shredded Oaxaca cheese, 2 tbsp chopped cilantro, red onion, and jalapeño (if using). The mixture should be thick but spoonable.

Using a measuring cup or ladle, spoon the salsa verde filling into the par-baked tortilla shells, about 3 tbsp per cup. The mixture should sit just below the top of the tortilla edges; gently nudge any stray tortilla strips back into cup shape so they bake into a cohesive rim.

Return the muffin tin to the oven and bake at 375°F for 13–15 minutes, until the filling is set in the center (it should not jiggle when you gently shake the pan) and the tortilla edges are deep golden and crisp. If any cups look pale at the edges, give them an extra 2–3 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and let the chilaquiles cups rest in the tin for 8–10 minutes. This rest is crucial so the tortilla shells firm up and the filling tightens enough to hold together.

Run a thin knife around the outer edge of each cup to release any stuck cheese or tortilla. Carefully lift each chilaquiles cup out by its crisp rim or slide a small offset spatula underneath to support the bottom. Transfer to a serving platter or plates.

Top each warm cup with a small spoonful of crumbled queso fresco, a few cubes of avocado, a drizzle of Mexican crema or sour cream, and a pinch of fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing over the top.

recipes.title: Spanakopita Phyllo Cups
recipes.description: These spanakopita cups tuck garlicky spinach, leeks, and salty feta into crisp, flaky phyllo that bakes into perfectly round, hand-held bites. The muffin wells shape the layered dough into sturdy little shells so you get shattering crunch around a soft, savory Greek-inspired filling. Ideal warm or at room temperature for lunches, mezze platters, or parties.
ingredients: 10 sheets phyllo dough, thawed (from a 16 oz package, 9x14 inch sheets)
6 tbsp unsalted butter, melted (plus more for greasing)
1 small leek, white and light green parts only, finely chopped (about 3/4 cup, rinsed well)
10 oz frozen chopped spinach, thawed and very well squeezed dry
1/4 cup fresh dill, finely chopped (or 2 tbsp dried dill)
1/2 tsp kosher salt (plus more to taste)
6 oz feta cheese, crumbled (preferably sheep’s milk)
1/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano or Kefalotyri
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Lightly brush a standard 12-cup muffin tin (all the wells and upper rims) with melted butter, making sure to get into the curves so the phyllo will crisp and release cleanly.

Set up a phyllo station: Unroll the thawed phyllo sheets on a clean counter. Cover them immediately with a sheet of plastic wrap and then a slightly damp kitchen towel so they don’t dry out. Keep your 6 tbsp melted butter nearby with a pastry brush.

Make the filling: In a medium skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped leek and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring often, until softened and just starting to turn golden at the edges, 5–7 minutes. Add the green onions and garlic; cook 1–2 minutes more until fragrant but not browned. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.

In a mixing bowl, combine the well-squeezed spinach (no excess moisture), cooled leek mixture, dill, parsley, nutmeg, 1/2 tsp salt, and black pepper. Stir to distribute the aromatics evenly through the spinach.

In a small bowl, whisk the eggs. Add the crumbled feta, grated Parmesan, and Greek yogurt; mix until you have a thick, slightly creamy mixture with visible feta chunks. Scrape this into the spinach mixture and fold together until everything is evenly combined. Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt if needed (keeping in mind the feta is salty).

Build the phyllo bases one cup at a time so they don’t dry out: Take 1 phyllo sheet from under the towel, lay it flat, and immediately cover the rest again. Lightly brush the sheet with melted butter all over (thin, even layer; don’t saturate). Stack a second sheet directly on top and brush again.

Using a sharp knife or pizza cutter, cut the buttered double-layer sheet into 6 equal rectangles (cut in half the long way, then into thirds the short way). Gently press one rectangle into a muffin well, centering it so the corners rise up past the rim and conform to the round shape of the well. Press it firmly against the bottom and sides so it hugs the curve of the cup. Repeat with a second rectangle in the same well, offsetting it so the corners don’t line up, creating a starburst of overhanging points. You now have 4 layers of phyllo forming a round shell.
Repeat Step 7 with the remaining phyllo sheets to line all 12 muffin wells with 4 layers each. If a sheet tears, just patch it in the cup with a buttered scrap—once baked, the layers will fuse.

Divide the spinach-feta filling evenly among the 12 phyllo-lined wells, about 2 heaping tablespoons per cup. The filling should sit just below the rim, with phyllo corners standing up around it. Gently fold some of the overhanging phyllo points inward over the filling, leaving a bit of the center exposed; brush any dry-looking tips lightly with remaining melted butter.

Bake on the middle rack at 375°F for 20–22 minutes, until the phyllo is deep golden brown and crisp and the filling is set and slightly puffed. If the outer phyllo edges brown too fast, lightly tent the pan with foil for the last few minutes.
Remove the pan to a wire rack and let the cups cool in the tin for 8–10 minutes. This rest lets the filling firm and the phyllo shells finish crisping so they hold their molded shape.

Run a thin knife around the sides of each cup, tracing the curve of the well to loosen any stuck bits. Lift each spanakopita cup straight up from the base—use the phyllo corners as little handles if needed—and transfer to a serving plate. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Paneer Saag Egg Bites
recipes.description: These paneer saag egg bites tuck spiced spinach, soft paneer, and a whisper of garam masala into tender, protein-rich cups that pop cleanly out of the pan. They eat like individual Indian-inspired frittatas, perfect with chutney for breakfast or a light lunch.
ingredients: 1 tbsp neutral oil (such as canola or avocado)
1 small serrano chile, seeded and finely minced (optional, for heat)
6 cups lightly packed baby spinach (roughly chopped)
4 oz paneer, cut into very small 1/4-inch cubes
1/2 cup whole milk plain yogurt (not Greek)
2 tbsp finely chopped fresh cilantro (plus extra for garnish, optional)
2 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint (optional but recommended)
2 tbsp finely grated Parmesan cheese (for a subtle savory boost)
Ghee or neutral oil, for greasing the muffin tin
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Position a rack in the center. Generously grease all 12 wells of a standard muffin tin with ghee or neutral oil, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms thoroughly so the bites release cleanly.

In a large skillet, heat 1 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp neutral oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook, stirring often, until soft and translucent, 4–5 minutes. Add the minced serrano (if using), ginger, and garlic; cook 1–2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.

Add the chopped spinach to the skillet in batches, stirring as it wilts. Sprinkle with 1/2 tsp kosher salt, turmeric, garam masala, cumin, and black pepper. Cook, stirring, until the spinach is fully wilted and most of the moisture has evaporated, 3–4 minutes. You want a relatively dry mixture so the bites set firmly. Remove from heat and let cool 5–10 minutes.
While the spinach mixture cools, place the paneer cubes in a small bowl. If they feel very firm or dry, sprinkle with 1 tbsp warm water and toss to soften slightly; drain off any excess water.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully combined and slightly frothy, about 30 seconds. Add the yogurt and whole milk and whisk until smooth with no visible lumps of yogurt. Whisk in 1/2 tsp kosher salt, cilantro, mint (if using), and Parmesan until evenly incorporated.

Stir the cooled spinach mixture into the egg mixture, breaking up any clumps so it’s evenly distributed. Fold in the paneer cubes gently so they stay fairly whole; you want some visible pieces in each bite.

Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 prepared muffin wells. Stir the bowl gently between scoops so the paneer and spinach don’t settle; each cup should get a good balance of egg, greens, and cheese. Fill each well nearly to the top, leaving about 1/8 inch space.

Bake at 350°F for 16–20 minutes, until the bites are puffed, the centers are just set, and a toothpick inserted in the center of one comes out mostly clean with only a few moist bits (no liquid egg). The tops may dome slightly; that’s good. Do not overbake or they’ll turn rubbery.

Remove the pan to a wire rack and let the bites cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes to firm up. Run a thin knife around the edges of each well to loosen, then gently lift each round egg bite out by the side, not the top, so they keep their molded shape.
Serve warm, garnished with extra cilantro if desired, with a side of cilantro-mint chutney or mango chutney for dipping.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Cups
recipes.description: These teriyaki salmon rice cups tuck soy-glazed salmon, sticky rice, and scallions into crisp-edged, molded rounds that lift cleanly from the pan. They eat like handheld sushi bowls with a glossy homemade teriyaki glaze, a touch of sesame, and a cool cucumber topping.
ingredients: 3/4 lb salmon fillet, skinless (center cut if possible)
1 tbsp neutral oil , plus extra for pan (canola or grapeseed)
2 tbsp sake (or additional mirin if unavailable)
2 tsp toasted sesame seeds (plus extra for garnish)
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold water, swishing with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear. Combine rinsed rice and 1 1/4 cups water in a small saucepan, bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to low, cover, and cook 15 minutes. Turn off heat and let sit, covered, 10 minutes.
While the rice cooks, preheat oven to 400°F. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with neutral oil, then mist generously with nonstick spray, making sure to coat the sides of each well.

In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook 4–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened and glossy. Remove from heat; set aside to cool slightly.

Pat the salmon dry and cut into 12 equal bite-size cubes (roughly 3/4 inch). Season lightly with 1/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Toss salmon pieces in 2 tbsp of the warm teriyaki sauce; set aside to marinate while you finish the rice.

In a small bowl, stir together 2 tbsp seasoned rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and 1 tsp sugar until dissolved. Transfer the hot cooked rice to a wide bowl. Drizzle the vinegar mixture over the rice and gently fold with a spatula or rice paddle, slicing through and turning to avoid mashing, until evenly seasoned. Let cool 10 minutes until just warm, not hot.

In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, 1 tbsp neutral oil, toasted sesame oil, scallions, and 2 tsp toasted sesame seeds. Add this mixture to the slightly cooled rice and gently fold to combine; the egg will help bind the cups so they hold their molded shape.

Divide the rice mixture evenly among the 12 muffin wells (about 2 heaping tbsp per cup). With damp fingers, press the rice firmly into each well, packing it down and slightly up the sides to form solid, round bases about 1/2 inch thick. Press well; the tighter the pack, the better they hold.

Place one teriyaki-coated salmon cube in the center of each rice base, pressing it gently into the rice so it nests but remains mostly exposed on top. Spoon an extra 1/4 to 1/2 tsp of teriyaki sauce over each salmon piece.

Bake at 400°F for 14–17 minutes, until the salmon is just cooked through and flakes easily, and the rice edges look set and lightly golden where they touch the pan. Do not overbake or the salmon will dry out.
While they bake, toss the diced cucumber with 1 tsp seasoned rice vinegar and 1/2 tsp soy sauce; set aside. If using, stir mayonnaise with a small squeeze of sriracha to make a thin drizzle.

Remove the pan from the oven and let the cups cool in the tin for 8–10 minutes to firm up. Run a thin knife around the edge of each well to loosen, then carefully lift each molded cup out with a small offset spatula or fork, keeping the round, flared shape intact.

Transfer to a serving plate. Top each cup with a pinch of marinated cucumber, a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, and a drizzle of teriyaki sauce and spicy mayo, if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Harissa Chickpea Feta Cups
recipes.description: These savory North African–inspired cups bake chickpeas, roasted peppers, and spinach into a softly set egg base with pockets of salty feta and smoky harissa heat. Each round, golden portion pops out of the tin as a complete protein-packed bite that reheats beautifully for weekday breakfasts or light lunches.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for greasing)
1 can chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted very dry (15 oz)
1/2 cup whole milk plain Greek yogurt
2 tbsp harissa paste (mild or hot, to taste)
1/2 tsp kosher salt (plus a pinch for veggies)
3 oz feta cheese, crumbled (about 3/4 cup, divided)
2 tbsp finely chopped fresh cilantro or flat-leaf parsley (plus more for garnish, optional)
2 tbsp fine dry breadcrumbs (plain or panko, lightly crushed)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with olive oil, making sure to coat the bottom and sides of each round well. Sprinkle a very light pinch of breadcrumbs into each cup, then tilt and tap so they lightly coat the bottom—this helps the cups release and gives a subtle crust.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and a small pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, 4–5 minutes. Add the red bell pepper and cook 2–3 minutes more until just tender.

Stir in the chopped spinach and cook, stirring, until wilted and most of the moisture has evaporated, 1–2 minutes. Remove from heat and let the mixture cool for 5 minutes so it doesn’t scramble the eggs.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until well combined and no streaks of white remain. Add the Greek yogurt and whisk until smooth, then whisk in the milk.
Whisk in the harissa paste, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, black pepper, cumin, and smoked paprika until the mixture is evenly tinted and the harissa is fully dispersed.

Add the chickpeas, cooled onion-pepper-spinach mixture, 1/2 cup of the feta, and 2 tbsp chopped cilantro or parsley to the egg mixture. Fold gently with a spatula so everything is evenly distributed but the chickpeas stay mostly whole.

Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 prepared muffin cups, making sure each round well gets a similar amount of chickpeas and vegetables. The cups should be filled to about 3/4 full. Sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup feta evenly over the tops.

Bake on the middle rack for 18–22 minutes, until the cups are puffed, set around the edges, and the centers barely jiggle when you gently shake the pan. A thin knife inserted near the center of a cup should come out mostly clean with just a bit of moisture, not liquid egg.

Remove the pan from the oven and let the cups cool in the tin for 8–10 minutes; this rest helps them firm and pull slightly from the sides so they release cleanly while keeping their molded, rounded shape.
Run a thin knife or offset spatula around the edge of each cup to loosen, then gently lift out. Serve warm, garnished with a little extra chopped cilantro or parsley if you like.

recipes.title: Roasted Broccoli Egg Cups
recipes.description: Tender baked egg cups packed with sharp cheese, roasted broccoli, and a touch of smoked paprika for warmth. They’re richly savory, beautifully set, and just as appealing at a leisurely brunch as they are straight from the fridge.
ingredients: 1 cup broccoli florets, small (fresh, tightly packed, cut to blueberry-size pieces)
3/4 tsp kosher salt (divided; 1/4 tsp for broccoli, 1/2 tsp for egg mixture)
3/8 tsp black pepper (divided; 1/8 tsp for broccoli, 1/4 tsp for egg mixture)
1/3 cup whole milk (or half-and-half for richer cups)
1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (lightly packed)
1/4 cup green onion, finely chopped (both white and green parts)
2 tbsp all-purpose flour (helps bind and hold shape)
as needed nonstick cooking spray (for greasing the pan)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Generously spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, making sure to coat the sides and rims of each cup.

Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp kosher salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper on a small sheet pan. Roast at 375°F for 8–10 minutes, until just tender and bright green with a few browned edges. Let cool slightly so they don’t scramble the eggs later.

In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until completely blended and no streaks remain—about 30 seconds of firm whisking. Whisk in the whole milk, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika until smooth.
Sprinkle the flour evenly over the egg mixture and whisk thoroughly until no lumps remain. This tiny bit of flour gives structure so the cups release cleanly and hold their shape instead of slumping.

Stir in the shredded cheddar, Parmesan, chopped green onion, parsley, and the roasted broccoli. Pour in the melted butter and gently fold everything together until evenly distributed. The mixture will look loose but with plenty of “bits” in every scoop.

Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 prepared muffin cups, stirring the bowl between scoops so the broccoli and cheese don’t settle. Each cup should be filled to about 3/4 full. If any cups look skimpy, steal a bit of filling from a fuller one so they bake evenly and hold together.

Place the muffin tin on the middle oven rack and bake at 375°F for 18–22 minutes, until the centers are just set, the tops are puffed, and the edges are lightly golden. A toothpick inserted in the center of a cup should come out mostly clean with just a bit of moisture, not wet egg.
Remove the pan from the oven and let the egg cups cool in the tin for 8–10 minutes. This rest is critical—cooling allows the proteins to set so the cups hold together when you remove them.

Run a small offset spatula or thin knife around the edges of each cup to loosen, then gently lift the egg cups out of the pan. Serve warm, or cool completely and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Savory Bacon Biscuit Rounds
recipes.description: These hearty biscuit rounds bake up as individual portions layered with smoky bacon, sharp cheddar, and scallions—sturdy enough for grab-and-go breakfasts all week. They reheat beautifully and eat like a cross between a biscuit and a breakfast sandwich without the fuss of assembly.
ingredients: 6 tbsp cold unsalted butter (cut into small cubes)
1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (packed, about 4 oz)
1/4 cup thinly sliced scallions (green and white parts)
3/4 cup cold buttermilk (shake well before measuring)
1 tbsp melted unsalted butter (for brushing tops)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Lightly spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, making sure to coat the sides of each cup.

Cook the bacon: Lay the bacon slices in a single layer in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook, turning occasionally, until crisp, 8–10 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel–lined plate to cool, then crumble or chop into small pieces. Reserve 1 tbsp of the rendered bacon fat from the pan and discard the rest.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder until well combined.

Add the cold cubed butter to the flour mixture. Using a pastry cutter or your fingertips, cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining. Don’t overwork it; you want visible bits of butter.
Stir in the shredded cheddar, sliced scallions, and crumbled bacon, tossing gently to distribute them evenly through the flour mixture.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, egg, Dijon mustard, honey, and the reserved 1 tbsp bacon fat until smooth and emulsified.

Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the buttermilk mixture. Using a rubber spatula, fold gently just until no dry pockets of flour remain. The dough will be thick and slightly sticky; avoid overmixing to keep the biscuits tender.

Divide the dough evenly among the 12 muffin cups, using about 1/4 cup of dough per cup. A lightly greased 1/4-cup measuring cup or scoop helps portion and press the dough in. Gently pat the tops to level them without compacting too much.
Brush the tops lightly with the 1 tbsp melted butter. Place the muffin tin on the middle rack of the oven.
Bake at 400°F for 15–18 minutes, until the tops are deep golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center of a biscuit round comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs (no wet batter).

Let the biscuit rounds cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then run a small offset spatula or butter knife around the edges to loosen and lift them out to a wire rack. Cool at least 10 more minutes before packing for storage, or serve warm.

recipes.title: Crispy Chorizo Breakfast Cups
recipes.description: Smoky chorizo, crisp golden hash browns, and a creamy pepper-jack egg custard bake into rich, savory little cups with a gentle kick and plenty of crunch in every bite.
ingredients: 3 cups frozen shredded hash brown potatoes (thawed and patted dry, plain not seasoned)
3/4 tsp kosher salt (divided; 1/2 tsp for potatoes, 1/4 tsp for egg mixture)
1/2 tsp black pepper (divided; 1/4 tsp for potatoes, 1/4 tsp for egg mixture)
8 oz fresh Mexican chorizo (raw, casings removed if linked)
1/2 cup whole milk (or half-and-half for richer cups)
1/2 cup shredded pepper jack cheese (lightly packed)
2 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped, optional, plus more for garnish)
to taste hot sauce or salsa (for serving, optional)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Use the unsalted butter to generously grease all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin, making sure to get the rims and top surface so nothing sticks where it overhangs.

Make the potato base: In a medium bowl, combine the thawed, well-dried frozen shredded hash brown potatoes, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt, 1/4 tsp of the black pepper, and the smoked paprika. Toss with your hands until every strand of potato is lightly coated.

Form the potato crusts: Divide the potato mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 1/4 cup loosely packed per cup). Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of each cup to form a nest, making sure there are no bare metal spots. Pack them a bit tighter on the bottom so they crisp instead of steaming.
Par-bake the potatoes: Bake the potato shells at 400°F for 12–14 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and starting to crisp. Remove from the oven but leave the oven on at 400°F.

Cook the chorizo filling: While the potatoes bake, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the fresh Mexican chorizo and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, for 4–5 minutes until mostly cooked through and starting to brown.

Add vegetables: Stir in the finely diced yellow onion and red bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes until the vegetables are softened and any excess moisture has mostly cooked off. Add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds more until fragrant. Remove from heat and let cool for 3–4 minutes so it doesn’t scramble the eggs later.

Make the egg mixture: In a medium bowl, whisk the large eggs until no streaks remain. Whisk in the whole milk, the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, the remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper, the ground cumin, and the chili powder until well combined. Stir in the shredded pepper jack cheese, shredded sharp cheddar cheese, and chopped fresh cilantro, making sure the cheese is evenly distributed.

Assemble the cups: Spoon the chorizo and vegetable mixture into the par-baked potato shells, dividing it evenly among all 12 cups (about 1 heaping tbsp per cup; don’t overfill above the rim). Give the egg mixture a quick stir, then pour it gently over the chorizo in each cup, filling to just below the top of the potato crust. Use a small spoon to nudge any trapped air bubbles out and ensure the egg mixture seeps down into the filling.

Bake: Return the muffin tin to the 400°F oven and bake for 14–16 minutes, until the egg is just set in the center and the tops are puffed and lightly golden. A toothpick inserted in the center of a cup should come out without wet egg, though a little moisture from melted cheese is fine.

Cool and release: Let the cups cool in the pan on a rack for 5–7 minutes to firm up. Run a thin offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup, then gently lift them out. If any cheese has stuck to the pan lip, loosen that before lifting so the crust doesn’t tear.

Serve or store: Serve warm, topped with extra cilantro, sliced green onions, and a dash of hot sauce or spoonful of salsa if you like. To store, cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Herbed Sausage Sunrise Cups
recipes.description: Crisp-edged sweet potato rounds cradle juicy turkey sausage, tender peppers, and a fluffy herb-flecked egg custard, all crowned with sharp cheddar and Parmesan. Each bite is rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying—perfect alongside hot coffee or a bright citrus salad.
ingredients: 1 lb orange sweet potato (peeled, about 2 medium)
8 oz mild turkey breakfast sausage (casings removed if linked)
1/2 cup whole milk (or half-and-half for richer texture)
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional, for mild heat)
3/4 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (preferably aged)
as needed cooking spray (for extra insurance, optional)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Use the butter to thoroughly grease all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin, making sure to coat the sides and rims. Lightly mist with cooking spray if your pan tends to stick; set aside.
Using the large holes of a box grater, grate the sweet potato into shreds. Pile the shreds on a clean kitchen towel and squeeze firmly over the sink to remove excess moisture.
In a medium bowl, toss the squeezed sweet potato with the olive oil, 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt, and 1/4 tsp of the black pepper until evenly coated.

Divide the sweet potato mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 2 heaping tbsp per cup). Use your fingers to press the shreds firmly onto the bottom and slightly up the sides to form thin rounds with shallow walls.
Bake the sweet potato bases at 400°F for 10–12 minutes, until they look slightly set and just starting to brown at the edges. Remove from the oven and reduce the oven temperature to 375°F.
While the bases bake, heat a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the turkey sausage and cook, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula, until no longer pink, 4–5 minutes.

Add the diced onion and both bell peppers to the skillet with the sausage. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and any excess moisture has cooked off, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds more. Remove from heat and let cool for 3–4 minutes.

In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until well blended and no streaks remain. Whisk in the milk, remaining 1/2 tsp kosher salt, remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper, parsley, chives, Italian seasoning, and crushed red pepper flakes, if using.
Stir the slightly cooled sausage mixture into the egg mixture. Fold in the shredded cheddar and grated Parmesan until evenly distributed.

Give the muffin tin a quick swipe with a paper towel if any oil pooled on the rims, then place it on a rimmed baking sheet for easier handling. Divide the egg-sausage mixture evenly among the 12 cups, filling each almost to the top. Stir the bowl occasionally as you pour so the solids stay evenly mixed.

Bake at 375°F for 18–20 minutes, until the centers are just set, the tops are puffed, and a toothpick inserted in the center of a cup comes out without wet egg (a bit of moisture from cheese is fine).

Let the cups cool in the pan for 5–7 minutes to firm up. Run a thin offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup, then gently lift out. Serve warm, or cool completely on a rack and enjoy at room temperature.

recipes.title: Smoky Sweet Potato Frittatas
recipes.description: Tender, custardy cups packed with caramelized sweet potato, smoky paprika, and sharp cheddar, these little frittatas taste like a pan of roasted vegetables wrapped in rich, savory eggs. A spoonful of Greek yogurt keeps them silky, while a tangle of greens and herbs adds fresh, gardeny flavor in every bite.
ingredients: 1 tbsp plus extra Olive oil (1 tbsp for vegetables, plus more for greasing muffin tin)
1 heaping cup Small sweet potato, peeled and diced 1/4 inch
3/4 cup Small red bell pepper, diced 1/4 inch
1 1/4 tsp Kosher salt (divided; 1/2 tsp for vegetables, 3/4 tsp for egg mixture)
3/4 tsp Black pepper (divided; 1/4 tsp for vegetables, 1/2 tsp for egg mixture)
1/2 cup Plain Greek yogurt (2% or whole)
1 cup Shredded sharp cheddar cheese (divided; 3/4 cup for egg mixture, 1/4 cup for topping)
2 tbsp Fresh parsley or chives, chopped (optional, for garnish)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with a little olive oil, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms of each cup.
In a medium bowl, toss the diced sweet potato, red bell pepper, zucchini, and red onion with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper until evenly coated.

Divide the vegetable mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 2 heaping tbsp per cup). The cups should be roughly 1/3 full. Bake for 12–14 minutes, until the sweet potato is just starting to soften and the edges of some vegetables are lightly golden.

While the vegetables roast, whisk the eggs in a large bowl until well combined and slightly frothy, 30–45 seconds. Add the Greek yogurt and whisk until completely smooth with no visible lumps, then whisk in the milk.

Season the egg mixture with the remaining 3/4 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, the garlic powder, smoked paprika, and dried thyme. Stir in the chopped spinach, 3/4 cup of the shredded cheddar, and the Parmesan until evenly distributed.

Remove the muffin tin from the oven. Using a small spoon, gently stir the vegetables in each cup to loosen any stuck bits. Give the egg mixture a quick stir, then immediately divide it evenly among the cups, pouring over the vegetables and filling each cup almost to the top.
Sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup shredded cheddar evenly over the tops of the cups.

Return the tin to the oven and bake at 375°F for 14–18 minutes, until the centers are just set and puffed and a toothpick inserted in the center of a cup comes out without wet egg (a little moisture is fine, but no liquid).

Let the frittata cups cool in the pan for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup to release, then gently lift out. Garnish with the chopped parsley or chives, if using, and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Maple Hash Brown Nests
recipes.description: These maple-scented hash brown nests bake up into crisp-edged, tender-centered portions that stay delicious for days. Shredded potatoes form a golden crust that cradles savory breakfast pork, peppers, and a just-set egg layer. They’re sturdy enough to grab on busy mornings, but nuanced enough in flavor that you’ll still look forward to them by Thursday.
ingredients: 8 oz maple breakfast sausage (pork), casings removed
1/2 cup red bell pepper, finely diced
1/4 cup green bell pepper, finely diced
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional, for mild heat)
1/3 cup sharp cheddar cheese, finely shredded
2 tbsp fresh chives, chopped (plus extra for garnish)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Generously spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, making sure to coat the top surface as well as the cups.

Shred the peeled russet potatoes on the large holes of a box grater. Pile the shreds into a clean kitchen towel, gather the towel, and twist firmly over the sink to squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer the dried potato shreds to a bowl. Add 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, and the melted unsalted butter. Toss with your fingers to coat evenly, breaking up any clumps.

Divide the potato mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 2 heaping tbsp per cup). Press firmly into the bottoms and up the sides to form little nests, making sure there are no gaps where egg could leak through.

Bake the potato shells at 400°F for 12–14 minutes, until the edges start to turn light golden and look set on the bottom. Remove from the oven but leave the oven on. If any potatoes have puffed up, gently press them back with the back of a spoon to re-form the wells.

While the shells bake, heat the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the maple breakfast sausage, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula. Cook 4–5 minutes until mostly browned and some fat has rendered.

Add the finely diced yellow onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4–5 minutes until the vegetables are softened and the sausage is nicely browned. Stir in the minced garlic, smoked paprika, crushed red pepper flakes (if using), and remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook 30 seconds more until fragrant, then remove from heat. Taste and add a pinch of kosher salt only if needed.

In a medium bowl, whisk the large eggs, whole milk, and remaining 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus a small pinch of black pepper, until fully combined and no streaks of yolk remain. Stir in the finely shredded sharp cheddar cheese, grated Parmesan cheese, and chopped fresh chives.
Spoon the sausage-and-pepper mixture into the pre-baked potato shells, dividing it evenly among all 12 cups and lightly pressing it down so it sits below the rim.

Give the egg mixture a quick whisk, then pour it over the sausage filling, filling each cup almost to the top but not overflowing. A small measuring cup or spouted pitcher makes this easier; stir between pours so the cheese and chives stay evenly distributed.

Return the muffin tin to the 400°F oven and bake 14–16 minutes, until the egg is just set in the center and a toothpick inserted into one cup comes out mostly clean with only a bit of moisture, no liquid. The tops will puff slightly and look matte, not shiny.

Set the pan on a wire rack and let the nests cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes to firm up. Run a thin knife around the edges of each one to loosen, then gently lift them out. Sprinkle with extra chopped chives before serving.

recipes.title: Prosciutto Potato Egg Nests
recipes.description: Shredded potatoes, caramelized onions, and sharp provolone are tucked into crisped prosciutto cups, then finished with a softly baked egg and chive-flecked cream. Salty, savory, and richly textured, these little nests bring serious brunch energy to any morning.
ingredients: 12 thin slices (about 6 oz) Prosciutto slices (not thick-cut)
3 cups Frozen shredded hash brown potatoes (thawed and well-drained)
1/2 cup Provolone cheese (finely grated, sharp, low-moisture)
2 tbsp Fresh chives (chopped, plus more for garnish, optional)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Place the oven rack in the center position. Lightly spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, making sure to coat the sides and rims of each cup.

Spread the frozen shredded hash brown potatoes on a plate or tray and let them stand at room temperature until fully thawed, 15–20 minutes. Once thawed, pat very dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture and set aside.

In a medium skillet, melt the butter with the olive oil over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onion and 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft and deeply golden, 10–12 minutes. If they start to brown too quickly, reduce the heat slightly. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.

In a medium bowl, combine the thawed, dried hash browns, black pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, provolone, Parmesan, and the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt. Add the slightly cooled caramelized onions and toss until everything is evenly distributed.

Line each muffin cup with a slice of prosciutto: press it gently into the bottom and up the sides, letting any excess rise above the rim to form a cup. If a slice tears, patch with a small piece from another slice—just avoid double-thick spots or they won’t crisp properly.

Divide the potato mixture evenly among the 12 prosciutto-lined cups, about 1/4 cup per cup. Press the mixture firmly into the bottom and up the sides to form a nest, leaving a shallow well in the center of each. Pack it tighter than you think; loose potatoes won’t crisp.

Bake the nests (without eggs yet) at 400°F for 15–18 minutes, until the prosciutto edges are crisping and the tops of the hash browns are lightly golden. If any potatoes puff up in the center, gently press them back down with the back of a spoon straight out of the oven to re-form the wells.

In a small bowl, whisk together the heavy cream and chopped chives. Crack one egg into a small ramekin or cup, then pour it gently into one of the hot nests. Spoon about 1 tsp of the chive cream over the yolk and white. Repeat with the remaining eggs and chive cream, working quickly so the nests don’t cool too much.

Return the muffin tin to the oven and bake at 400°F for 9–12 minutes, depending on how runny you like your yolks. Start checking at 9 minutes: the whites should be just set and opaque, and the yolks should still have a slight wobble. For firmer yolks, go closer to 12 minutes.

Remove the tin from the oven and let the nests cool in the pan for 5 minutes to firm up. Run a thin knife around the edges of each cup to loosen, then lift out carefully with a small offset spatula or fork.

Garnish with extra chopped chives if desired. Serve warm, or let cool completely and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat individual nests on a sheet pan at 350°F for 8–10 minutes.

recipes.title: Mini Caprese Bruschetta Bites
recipes.description: All the flavors of a classic caprese bruschetta—garlic toast, juicy tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil—baked into tidy, handheld muffin tin bites. A buttery Parmesan bread base crisps in the oven, then gets filled with a warm caprese mixture and finished with a sweet-tart balsamic drizzle. Ideal as a party appetizer or light summer snack.
ingredients: 4 tbsp unsalted butter (melted, plus extra for greasing)
3 cups small-dice day-old Italian or French bread (about 6 oz, crusts on)
1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese (preferably Parmigiano-Reggiano)
1 cup halved cherry or grape tomatoes (preferably mixed colors)
1 cup small fresh mozzarella pearls (ciliegine or perlini, drained)
1/4 cup thinly sliced fresh basil leaves (plus extra for garnish)
Optional: pinch of crushed red pepper flakes (for heat)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin with butter, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms well.
In a large bowl, combine the melted butter and 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the diced bread and toss until every piece is lightly coated. Let sit 3–4 minutes so the bread absorbs the fat.

Add the Parmesan, 1/4 tsp kosher salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper to the bread and toss again. In a small bowl, whisk together the egg and milk, then pour over the bread mixture and fold gently until the bread is evenly moistened but not soggy.

Divide the bread mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 1/4 cup per cup). Press firmly with your fingers or the back of a spoon to compact and push some of the mixture slightly up the sides to form shallow “toast” cups.
Bake the bread bases for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are golden and starting to crisp. Remove from the oven but leave the oven on. Let the cups cool in the pan for 5 minutes to set.

While the bases bake, make the caprese filling: In a medium bowl, combine the tomatoes, mozzarella pearls, red onion, basil, minced garlic, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar, remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, remaining 1/8 tsp black pepper, and crushed red pepper flakes if using. Toss gently to coat without breaking up the tomatoes.

Spoon the caprese mixture into the partially baked bread cups, dividing evenly among all 12. Try to get a mix of tomato and mozzarella in each cup; you’ll use most of the liquid but avoid overfilling to the point of overflowing.
Return the muffin tin to the oven and bake for 8–10 minutes, until the mozzarella is just melted and the bread edges are deep golden and crisp.

Remove from the oven and let the bites rest in the pan for 5 minutes; this helps them hold together. Run a small offset spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup and gently lift the bites out onto a serving platter.
Drizzle each bite lightly with balsamic glaze and garnish with a few extra basil ribbons. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Smoky Cheddar Breakfast Bites
recipes.description: Little golden bites packed with tender vegetables, sharp cheddar, Parmesan, and a whisper of smoked paprika, these savory muffins bring all the cozy flavors of a loaded frittata in handheld form. They’re rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying—perfect with hot coffee, a splash of hot sauce, or tucked into a warm, toasty English muffin.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil (1 tbsp for sautéing vegetables, plus extra for greasing the muffin tin)
as needed nonstick cooking spray (for greasing the muffin tin)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Place an oven thermometer in the center if you have one and let the oven fully preheat. Lightly spray a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray, then rub each cup with a thin film of olive oil to ensure good release.

Warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the broccoli, red bell pepper, and yellow onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and lightly fragrant, 5–6 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Stir the grape tomatoes and chopped baby spinach into the warm vegetables. The spinach should just begin to wilt. Set aside to cool slightly while you prepare the eggs.

In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until completely blended and no streaks of white remain, about 30–45 seconds. Add the milk, kosher salt, black pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and dried thyme. Whisk again until the mixture looks uniform and lightly frothy.
Fold the shredded sharp cheddar and grated Parmesan into the egg mixture until evenly distributed.

Divide the sautéed vegetable mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 2 heaping tablespoons per cup). Stir the egg mixture briefly, then pour it over the vegetables, filling each cup almost to the top but not overflowing. Use a spoon to gently nudge the vegetables so they’re submerged and evenly spread.

Place the muffin tin on the middle rack and bake at 350°F for 18–22 minutes, until the breakfast bites are puffed, set in the center, and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out without wet egg. The tops may have a light golden edge.

Remove the pan from the oven and let the bites cool in the tin for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup, then gently lift out the bites and transfer to a wire rack to cool completely if storing.
For storage, refrigerate the cooled breakfast bites in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or wrap each one tightly in plastic wrap and then place in a freezer bag to freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Roasted Veggie Egg Cups
recipes.description: These roasted veggie egg prep cups are built for grab-and-go breakfasts all week: high-protein, packed with vegetables, and they reheat beautifully. Roasting the vegetables first concentrates their flavor so the eggs don’t taste like a sad hotel buffet. Make a pan on Sunday and you’ve got breakfast handled through Friday.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for greasing)
1 cup small broccoli florets (fresh, not frozen)
4 large egg whites (about 1/2 cup, from carton or separated)
1/2 cup 2% milk (or whole milk for richer cups)
Nonstick cooking spray (canola or avocado oil)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Place an oven thermometer inside; don’t trust the dial. Lightly coat a standard 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray, then rub each cup with a bit of olive oil to be sure every corner is coated.

On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the broccoli, red bell pepper, onion, and zucchini with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Spread in an even layer, keeping vegetables in a single layer so they roast, not steam.

Roast the vegetables at 400°F for 12–15 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until they’re just tender and starting to brown at the edges. Remove from the oven and let cool 5 minutes so they don’t scramble the eggs on contact.

Reduce oven temperature to 350°F. In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, egg whites, milk, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and Parmesan. Whisk until the mixture is completely uniform and no streaks of egg white remain.

Stir 1/4 cup of the shredded cheddar and the chopped parsley into the cooled roasted vegetables. Divide the vegetable mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups (about 2 heaping tablespoons per cup). Gently press the vegetables down so they form an even layer.

Transfer the muffin tin to the oven rack (this minimizes sloshing), then carefully pour the egg mixture into each cup, filling each about 3/4 full. Stir the egg mixture between pours so the seasonings stay evenly distributed.

Sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup shredded cheddar evenly over the tops of the cups. Bake at 350°F for 16–18 minutes, until the centers are just set and a toothpick inserted in the center of a cup comes out mostly clean with a few moist bits, but no liquid.

Remove the tin from the oven and let the egg cups cool in the pan for 5–10 minutes. Run a thin knife or offset spatula around the edges of each cup and gently lift them out. Serve warm, or cool completely for storage.

recipes.title: Roasted Veggie Frittata Cups
recipes.description: These muffin tin frittatas are packed with roasted vegetables, sharp cheese, and herbs for a make-ahead breakfast that actually tastes like something you’d order at a café. They reheat beautifully all week, stay tender instead of rubbery, and are endlessly adaptable to whatever’s in your crisper drawer. Make a pan on Sunday and you’ve got grab-and-go protein portions ready to go.
ingredients: 1 tbsp unsalted butter (for greasing muffin tin)
1 cup small broccoli florets (cut into 1/2-inch pieces)
3/4 cup red bell pepper, diced (1/4-inch pieces)
1/3 cup whole milk (or half-and-half for richer texture)
1/8 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (optional, for mild heat)
1/2 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (Tillamook or similar)
1 tbsp chopped fresh chives (or green onion tops)
1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese (for topping)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Place the oven rack in the center position. Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with the 1 tbsp unsalted butter, making sure to coat the sides and bottoms of each cup thoroughly.

In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the broccoli, red bell pepper, onion, and mushrooms. Sprinkle with 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt and a pinch (about 1/8 tsp) of black pepper. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and any mushroom moisture has cooked off, 6–8 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool 5 minutes.

In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until the whites and yolks are completely blended and slightly frothy, about 30 seconds. Add the whole milk, remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt, remaining black pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and crushed red pepper flakes (if using). Whisk until well combined.

Fold the cooled vegetable mixture into the eggs. Add the shredded sharp cheddar, crumbled feta, chopped parsley, and chives. Stir with a spatula until everything is evenly distributed—no big clumps of vegetables or cheese.

Place the greased muffin tin on a rimmed baking sheet (this makes it easier to move and catches any spills). Divide the egg mixture evenly among the 12 cups, filling each about 3/4 full. The solids will want to sink; use a spoon to pull some vegetables and cheese into each cup so they’re evenly loaded.
Sprinkle the tops of each cup with the grated Parmesan, dividing it evenly. Gently tap the baking sheet on the counter once or twice to settle the mixture and release large air bubbles.

Bake at 375°F for 18–22 minutes, until the frittata cups are puffed, set in the center, and just barely jiggle when you nudge the pan. A toothpick inserted in the center of a cup should come out mostly clean with no wet egg.

Remove the muffin tin from the oven and let the frittata cups cool in the pan for 5–7 minutes. Run a thin spatula or butter knife around the edges of each cup to loosen, then gently lift out and transfer to a cooling rack.

Serve warm, or let cool completely before refrigerating in an airtight container for up to 5 days. To reheat, warm 1–2 frittata cups in the microwave for 20–30 seconds, or in a 325°F oven for 8–10 minutes until heated through.

recipes.title: Mini Lemon Meringue Cups
recipes.description: These mini lemon meringue cups give you all the bright, tart snap of a classic lemon meringue pie in crisp, buttery, handheld portions. A shortbread-style crust, sharp lemon curd, and toasted marshmallowy meringue are built right in a standard 12-cup muffin tin—no tart rings, no drama.
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold, cut into 1/2-inch cubes (113 g / 1 stick)
3 large egg yolks, room temperature (reserve 3 of the whites for meringue)
1/2 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice (120 ml)
1 Tbsp finely grated lemon zest (from unsprayed lemons)
4 Tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces (56 g)
3 large egg whites , room temperature (from above)
1–2 Tbsp very soft unsalted butter (for greasing)
instructions: **Prepare the muffin tin and preheat oven**
- Generously grease all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin with very soft butter, making sure to coat the sides and corners well. Dust lightly with flour, tapping out the excess.
- Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Place an oven rack in the middle position.
**Make the crust dough**
- In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, powdered sugar, and salt.
- Add the cold butter cubes. Using your fingertips or a pastry cutter, work the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized bits of butter remaining.
- In a small bowl, whisk together egg yolk and vanilla. Drizzle over the flour mixture and gently toss with a fork until it starts to clump.
- Use your hands to press the mixture together into a soft dough; it should hold when squeezed. If it’s too dry and crumbly, add 1 teaspoon cold water and work it in lightly.
**Portion and form the crusts**
- Divide the dough into 12 equal portions (about 20–22 g each; or eyeball, then adjust).

- Roll each portion into a ball, then press into the bottom and up the sides of each muffin cup, aiming for an even thickness about 1/8 inch. Take your time; thin, even walls bake more evenly than thick clumps at the bottom.
- Prick the bottoms lightly with a fork (2–3 times per cup) to reduce puffing.
**Blind-bake the crusts**
- Bake the crusts at 350°F (175°C) for 12–14 minutes, until they are just set and lightly golden at the edges.
- If any bottoms have puffed, gently press them back down with the back of a spoon while still hot.
- Reduce oven temperature to 325°F (165°C). Leave oven on.
**Make the lemon filling**
- While the crusts bake, in a medium, heavy-bottomed saucepan, whisk together whole eggs, egg yolks, sugar, lemon juice, lemon zest, and salt until smooth and thoroughly combined.

- Place the pan over medium-low heat. Cook, whisking constantly (really, don’t stop), until the mixture thickens to the consistency of loose pudding and reaches 170–175°F (77–80°C), 6–10 minutes depending on your stove. Do not let it boil hard.
- Remove from heat. Add butter pieces and whisk until completely melted and the curd is glossy and smooth.
